mainTopic: The congregation's responses during ברכת כהנים and מודים, stories of humility, and respect for the congregation
overview: The גמרא asks what the people say while the כהנים bless them at נעילה on יום כיפור. The answer is three פסוקים from תהלים. The אמוראים then disagree about when to say them and how many to say each time. Some say these פסוקים should not be said at all, outside the מקדש or even inside it, because someone being blessed should listen. רבי אחא בר חנינא says they should be said everywhere. רבי אבהו stopped saying them after seeing רבי אבא דמן עכו, and this leads into stories about the humility of both scholars. Next the גמרא lists the words the people say during the שליח ציבור's מודים, and רב פפא rules that we say all of them together. Then the גמרא looks for sources that one must respect the congregation, and רב אשי rejects one of the proofs. The amud ends by quoting the next line of the משנה: in the מקדש, ברכת כהנים is one blessing.

steps.title: What is said at נעילה of יום כיפור?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the congregation says during ברכת כהנים at נעילה on יום כיפור.
steps.simpleTranslation: At the closing prayer of יום כיפור, what do the people say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is asking a question. It is setting up the next step, where we will hear which פסוקים the people say during נעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נעילה also has ברכת כהנים, so the גמרא wants to know which פסוקים the congregation says while the כהנים are blessing them at that time.

keyTerms.meaning: The closing prayer at the end of יום כיפור

phrases.english: At the closing prayer of Yom Kippur,
what does one say?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the discussion in this section
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which words the congregation says during ברכת כהנים at נעילה

steps.title: Three פסוקים from תהלים
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא, or a ברייתא according to another version, says the people say three פסוקים from תהלים קכ״ח.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא says, and some say it was taught in a ברייתא: "Behold, this is how a man who fears ה׳ is blessed." "ה׳ will bless you from Zion, and you will see the good of Jerusalem all the days of your life." "And see children of your children, peace upon Israel."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. At נעילה the people say three פסוקים about blessing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three פסוקים speak about being blessed, so they fit the moment the כהנים are blessing the people. There are two versions of who said this: מר זוטרא himself, or a ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (another version of who said it)
A ברייתא, a teaching of the תנאים outside the משנה

phrases.english: Mar Zutra says,
and some say it in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: ״הִנֵּה כִי כֵן יְבֹרַךְ גָּבֶר יְרֵא ה׳״.
phrases.english: "Behold, surely thus shall the man who fears the Lord be blessed."
"The Lord shall bless you out of Zion,

phrases.aramaic: וּרְאֵה בְּטוּב יְרוּשָׁלִָם כֹּל יְמֵי חַיֶּיךָ״.
phrases.english: and you shall see the good of Jerusalem all the days of your life."
"And see your children's children.
Peace be upon Israel."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ בְּמַתְנִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1

steps.title: When are these verses said?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks at which point during ברכת כהנים the people say these פסוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where in the blessing does one say them?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know what is said, the גמרא asks when. This sets up a disagreement in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ברכת כהנים has three parts. The question is where in those parts the congregation fits in its פסוקים.

phrases.english: Where does one say them?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכָן אוֹמְרָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the answer of step 2
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact point in ברכת כהנים when the פסוקים are said

steps.title: Between blessings or at God's name
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says between each blessing. רב ששת says when the כהנים mention ה׳'s name.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף says: between each and every blessing. And רב ששת says: at the mention of the Name.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two answers to the question of when. They disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף says the people wait for a break between the three blessings. רב ששת says they say them when the כהנים say ה׳'s name in each blessing, which is earlier, in the middle of the blessing.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef says:
between each and every blessing.
And Rav Sheshet says:
at the mention of the Name.
phrases.notes: That's when the כהנים say ה׳'s name in each of the three blessings.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3 with two opinions
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב יוסף: between blessings; רב ששת: at the mention of the Name

steps.title: One verse each time, or all three
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי and רב זביד argue whether the people say one פסוק for each blessing, or all three פסוקים each time.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרי and רב זביד disagree about it. One says: one פסוק matching one פסוק. And one says: for each פסוק, he says all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new disagreement about how the פסוקים are spread out over the blessing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ברכת כהנים has three פסוקים and the people have three פסוקים. One view matches them up, one for one. The other view says the people repeat all three after each of the כהנים' פסוקים.
steps.confusionAlert: We are not told which of the two holds which view; the גמרא only says "one says" and "one says".

phrases.aramaic: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַב מָרִי וְרַב זְבִיד.
phrases.english: Rav Mari and Rav Zevid disagree about it.
One says: a verse corresponding to a verse.
phrases.notes: Each of the people's פסוקים goes with one of the three פסוקים the כהנים say.

phrases.english: And one says:
for every verse, he says all of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַב מָרִי וְרַב זְבִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another detail about how the פסוקים are said
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dispute: one פסוק per blessing, or all three after each blessing
steps.whatToRemember: Two disputes about timing: where (between blessings or at ה׳'s name), and how many (one פסוק each time or all three each time).

steps.title: Saying them outside the מקדש is a mistake
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא says anyone who says these פסוקים outside the מקדש is mistaken.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא says: Anyone who says them in the outlying areas is simply mistaken.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement limiting the practice: it does not belong outside the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now it sounded like everyone says these פסוקים. Now רבי חייא בר אבא says that outside the מקדש this practice is wrong.

phrases.english: Rabbi Hiyya bar Abba says:
Anyone who says them in the outlying areas
is nothing other than mistaken.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא: כׇּל הָאוֹמְרָן בַּגְּבוּלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the practice described in steps 2–5
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Saying these פסוקים outside the מקדש is a mistake

steps.title: Not even in the מקדש: a servant should listen
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בר פפא says even in the מקדש these פסוקים should not be said, because one being blessed should listen.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא בר פפא said: Know that even in the מקדש they should not be said. Is there a servant who is being blessed and does not listen?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא בר פפא goes further than step 6 and gives a reason with a simple example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a servant is being blessed, he should be quiet and listen, not talk over the blessing. So the people should listen to the כהנים and not say פסוקים, even in the מקדש.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that while the כהנים bless, the people's main job is to listen to the ברכה.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי חייא בר אבא: outside the מקדש it is a mistake. רבי חנינא בר פפא: even in the מקדש don't say them, because someone being blessed should listen.

phrases.english: Rabbi Hanina bar Pappa said:
Know that in the Temple also
one should not say them.
Do you have a servant
who is being blessed and does not listen?

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּדַּע דִּבְמִקְדָּשׁ נָמֵי לָא מִיבְּעֵי לְמֵימְרִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes further than step 6, extending it to the מקדש with a reason
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even in the מקדש the people should not say these פסוקים, because one being blessed must listen

steps.title: The people should say the פסוקים outside the מקדש too
steps.stepSummary: רבי אחא בר חנינא holds that the פסוקים should be said even in the גבולין, because one who is blessed should respond warmly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אחא בר חנינא says: You should know that even outside the מקדש people must say these פסוקים. Is there a servant who is blessed and does not respond with a happy face?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אחא בר חנינא gives the opposite view from the last two steps. He says the people should say these פסוקים even outside the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא בר אבא said saying them outside the מקדש is a mistake. רבי חנינא בר פפא said one being blessed should just listen. רבי אחא בר חנינא argues the other way: when a servant receives a blessing, he should show thanks, so saying the פסוקים is a proper response.

keyTerms.meaning: You should know (introduces a reason or proof)

phrases.english: Rabbi Aḥa bar Ḥanina says:
Know that in the outlying areas also
one needs to say them,
phrases.notes: "Them" means the פסוקים the people say during ברכת כהנים.

phrases.english: Is there a servant who is being blessed
and does not show a bright face?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַחָא בַּר חֲנִינָא: תֵּדַע דְּבִגְבוּלִין נָמֵי מִיבְּעֵי לְמֵימְרִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite opinion to steps 6 and 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוקים should be said even in the גבולין, as a grateful response to being blessed.

steps.title: רבי אבהו stopped saying the פסוקים
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו used to say the פסוקים. He stopped after he saw that רבי אבא דמן עכו did not say them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו says: At first I used to say them. But since I saw that רבי אבא דמן עכו does not say them, I also do not say them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו tells us what he did in practice. He followed the example of רבי אבא דמן עכו and stopped saying the פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a report of real practice, not a new argument. It sides with the view that the פסוקים should not be said. It also brings in רבי אבא דמן עכו, the person the coming stories will focus on.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu says:
At first I would say them,
since I saw
Rabbi Abba of Akko
that he does not say them —
I also do not say them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: מֵרֵישׁ הֲוָה אָמֵינָא לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reports a practice that goes against רבי אחא בר חנינא's view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In practice, רבי אבהו did not say the פסוקים, following רבי אבא דמן עכו.
steps.whatToRemember: Two sides: רבי חייא בר אבא and רבי חנינא בר פפא say not to recite the פסוקים, and רבי אבהו followed this in practice. רבי אחא בר חנינא says to recite them even outside the מקדש.

steps.title: רבי אבהו learns how humble רבי אבא דמן עכו was
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו thought he was humble. Then he saw that רבי אבא דמן עכו did not mind when his אמורא gave a different reason than his own.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו also said: At first I thought I was humble. But I saw that רבי אבא דמן עכו gave one reason, and his אמורא gave a different reason, and he did not mind. Then I said: I am not humble.
steps.whatsHappening: Having mentioned רבי אבא דמן עכו, the גמרא moves into a story about him. רבי אבהו praises his great humility.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אמורא was the speaker who repeated the teacher's words aloud to the crowd. Here the אמורא swapped in his own reason, and רבי אבא was not bothered at all. Seeing this, רבי אבהו decided his own humility was small next to that.

keyTerms.meaning: The speaker who repeats the teacher's words aloud to the crowd

phrases.english: And Rabbi Abbahu says:
At first I would say: I am humble.

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דַּחֲזֵינָא לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי אַבָּא דְּמִן עַכּוֹ
phrases.english: Since I saw Rabbi Abba of Akko
that he himself said one reason
and his interpreter said a different reason
and he did not mind —
I say: I am not humble.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: מֵרֵישׁ הֲוָה אָמֵינָא עִינְוְתָנָא אֲנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the mention of רבי אבא דמן עכו to begin a set of stories about humility.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אבא דמן עכו's humility was so great that רבי אבהו saw himself as not humble.

steps.title: What did רבי אבהו's humility look like?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what humility רבי אבהו had, since he said he used to think he was humble.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what was the humility of רבי אבהו?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question to set up the next stories. It wants to see the humility רבי אבהו thought he had.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבהו said he once thought he was humble. The גמרא asks what that humility was, so we can see how great רבי אבא's humility must have been to outshine it.

phrases.english: And what was the humility of Rabbi Abbahu?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי עִינְוְותָנוּתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for an example of the humility רבי אבהו mentioned in step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A real example of רבי אבהו's humility.

steps.title: רבי אבהו does not care who gets the credit
steps.stepSummary: The wife of רבי אבהו's אמורא boasted that her husband did not need רבי אבהו. רבי אבהו answered that through both of them, ה׳ is praised.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wife of רבי אבהו's אמורא said to רבי אבהו's wife: "My husband does not need yours. When he bends down to hear him and stands up to speak, he is only showing respect." רבי אבהו's wife told him this. He answered her: "What difference does it make to you? Through me and through him, ה׳ above is praised."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a story. רבי אבהו was not insulted by a put-down and said that only ה׳'s honor matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The insult was that the אמורא could teach on his own and only acted as רבי אבהו's speaker out of respect. רבי אבהו did not defend his own importance. His only concern was that Torah was taught and ה׳ was praised, no matter who did it.

phrases.aramaic: דַּאֲמַרָה לַהּ דְּבֵיתְהוּ דְּאָמוֹרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ
phrases.english: For the wife of Rabbi Abbahu's interpreter said
to Rabbi Abbahu's wife:

phrases.aramaic: הָא דִּידַן לָא צְרִיךְ לֵיהּ לְדִידָךְ,
phrases.english: This one of ours does not need yours,
phrases.notes: "Ours" is her husband, the אמורא. "Yours" is רבי אבהו.

phrases.english: and the fact that he bends down and stands up over him —
phrases.notes: He bends down to hear רבי אבהו quietly, then stands up to say it aloud to the crowd.

phrases.english: it is merely honor that he does for him.

phrases.aramaic: אֲזַלָא דְּבֵיתְהוּ וַאֲמַרָה לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ.
phrases.english: His wife went and told Rabbi Abbahu.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לַהּ: וּמַאי נָפְקָא לִיךְ מִינַּהּ?
phrases.english: He said to her: And what difference does it make to you?
Through me and through him the One above will be praised.

steps.triggerLanguage: דַּאֲמַרָה לַהּ דְּבֵיתְהוּ דְּאָמוֹרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11 with a story.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אבהו was not bothered by an insult that his אמורא did not need him, because ה׳ is praised through both of them.

steps.title: רבי אבהו gives up the head position for רבי אבא דמן עכו
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים decided to appoint רבי אבהו as head. He saw that רבי אבא דמן עכו had many creditors, so he said there was someone greater.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore: The חכמים decided to appoint רבי אבהו as head. Since he saw that רבי אבא דמן עכו had many people he owed money to, he said to them: "There is someone greater."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second example of רבי אבהו's humility. He turned down a position of leadership so that a poor scholar could have it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "ותו" adds a further answer to the question in step 11. רבי אבהו gave the honor to רבי אבא דמן עכו, who was deep in debt, calling him greater. This shows humility together with care for a struggling colleague.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אבהו showed humility twice. He did not care who got credit for teaching, and he gave up the head position to רבי אבא דמן עכו. Even so, he said רבי אבא's humility was greater than his own.

phrases.english: And furthermore,
Rabbi Abbahu — the Sages were counted regarding him
phrases.notes: The חכמים took a count and agreed to choose him.

phrases.english: to appoint him as head,

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּחַזְיֵהּ לְרַבִּי אַבָּא דְּמִן עַכּוֹ
phrases.english: since he saw Rabbi Abba of Akko
that he had many creditors,
he said to them: There is a greater one.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ, רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אִימְּנוֹ רַבָּנַן עֲלֵיהּ לְמִמְנְיֵיהּ בְּרֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second example answering the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אבהו gave up being appointed head in favor of רבי אבא דמן עכו, who was in debt.

steps.title: Everyone leaves רבי חייא בר אבא's class for רבי אבהו's
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו taught אגדה and רבי חייא בר אבא taught הלכה in the same town. Everyone went to רבי אבהו, and רבי חייא בר אבא was hurt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו and רבי חייא בר אבא came to a certain place. רבי אבהו taught אגדה, and רבי חייא בר אבא taught הלכה. Everyone left רבי חייא בר אבא and went to רבי אבהו. רבי חייא בר אבא felt hurt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more story about the humility of רבי אבהו. This step only sets up the problem. The next step shows how he responded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the answer to the question in step 11 about what humility רבי אבהו had. The scene is set: two teachers, two kinds of Torah, and one of them ends up embarrassed. The real test of humility comes in how רבי אבהו handles it.

keyTerms.meaning: אגדה: stories, lessons and non-legal Torah teaching
a הלכה lesson: legal Torah teaching

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ וְרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא
phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu and Rabbi Chiya bar Abba
happened to come to a certain place.
Rabbi Abbahu taught אגדה,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא דְּרַשׁ בִּשְׁמַעְתָּא.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Chiya bar Abba taught הלכה.

phrases.aramaic: שַׁבְקוּהּ כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לְרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא,
phrases.english: Everyone left Rabbi Chiya bar Abba
and went to Rabbi Abbahu.
He felt hurt.
phrases.notes: That's רבי חייא בר אבא, the one whose class was left empty.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ וְרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אִיקְּלַעוּ לְהָהוּא אַתְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another story showing רבי אבהו's humility, after the story about the חכמים appointing him head.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A further example of רבי אבהו's humility begins: he is about to comfort a colleague whose class was emptied because of him.

steps.title: The parable of the jewel seller and the cheap goods seller
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו comforts רבי חייא בר אבא. He says people crowd around the seller of cheap small items, not the seller of precious stones.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said to him: Let me give you a parable. Picture two people. One sells precious stones and one sells small cheap items. Whom do customers rush to? Isn't it the one selling the small items?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו makes his own teaching sound smaller so that רבי חייא בר אבא will feel better.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Your הלכה is like precious jewels: valuable, but few people can buy them. My אגדה is like cheap goods, so everyone crowds around it. Here is the humility: רבי אבהו lowers himself to raise his colleague.

keyTerms.meaning: small cheap items, like needles and trinkets

phrases.english: He said to him: I will tell you a parable.
What is this like?
To two people.
One sells precious stones,
and one sells all kinds of small items.
Whom do people rush to?

phrases.aramaic: לֹא עַל זֶה שֶׁמּוֹכֵר מִינֵי סִידְקִית?
phrases.english: Isn't it to the one who sells small items?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶמְשֹׁל לְךָ מָשָׁל לְמָה הַדָּבָר דּוֹמֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי אבהו's response to רבי חייא בר אבא's hurt feelings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Crowds go to the easy, cheap thing. That says nothing about which teaching is more valuable. Deeper הלכה is like jewels.

steps.title: רבי אבהו escorts רבי חייא בר אבא home
steps.stepSummary: Usually רבי חייא בר אבא escorted רבי אבהו because of his ties to the government. That day רבי אבהו escorted him instead, but he was still not fully calmed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Every day, רבי חייא בר אבא would walk רבי אבהו to his lodging, out of respect for the emperor's household. That day, רבי אבהו walked רבי חייא בר אבא to his lodging. Even so, רבי חייא בר אבא was still not at peace with him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו reverses the usual honor and escorts his colleague home to make peace. The story ends by saying the hurt was not fully healed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the honor went to רבי אבהו because of his standing with the Roman government. By switching roles, he showed real humility. The ending is honest: even a kind act does not always erase hurt feelings.

keyTerms.meaning: escorting, walking someone on his way
the honor of the emperor's household
his mind was put at ease

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אבהו's humility shows in how he treats others. He let his אמורא's wife boast, turned down being head for someone poorer, made his own Torah sound small, and escorted a colleague home.

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל יוֹמָא: הֲוָה מַלְוֵה רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא
phrases.english: Every day, Rabbi Chiya bar Abba would escort
Rabbi Abbahu to his lodging place,
out of respect for the emperor's household.
phrases.notes: רבי אבהו was close to the Roman government, so people honored him for that.

phrases.english: That day, Rabbi Abbahu escorted

phrases.aramaic: לְרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא עַד אוּשְׁפִּיזֵיהּ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya bar Abba to his lodging place.

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲפִילּוּ הָכִי לָא אִיתּוֹתַב דַּעְתֵּיהּ מִינֵּיהּ.
phrases.english: Even so, his mind was not at ease with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל יוֹמָא הֲוָה מַלְוֵה רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא לְרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same story with a second act of humility, and closes the stories about רבי אבהו.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אבהו gave up his usual honor to make peace, even though רבי חייא בר אבא remained hurt.

steps.title: What do the people say during מודים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to תפילה. It asks what the congregation says while the שליח ציבור says the blessing of מודים.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the שליח ציבור says מודים, what do the people say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the stories and starts a new topic about the congregation's response in חזרת הש״ץ. This question sets up a list of answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same kind of question as at the start of the amud: what the congregation says while someone else is saying a part of the תפילה. Here the part is מודים, the blessing of thanks, and the גמרא wants the exact words.

keyTerms.meaning: the thanksgiving blessing in the עמידה

phrases.english: When the prayer leader says מודים,
what do the people say?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּזְמַן שֶׁשְּׁלִיחַ צִבּוּר אוֹמֵר מוֹדִים הָעָם מָה הֵם אוֹמְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the stories about רבי אבהו and goes back to the congregation's responses during תפילה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The wording the congregation says during the שליח ציבור's מודים.

steps.title: רב's wording
steps.stepSummary: רב says the people say: We thank You, ה׳ our God, for being able to thank You.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: We give thanks to You, ה׳ our God, for the fact that we give thanks to You.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the first answer to the question. רב gives a short thank-you formula.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ending 'על שאנו מודים לך' means we even thank ה׳ for the gift of being able to thank Him. This ending repeats in every opinion that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: for the fact that we thank You

steps.confusionAlert: Every opinion that follows ends with the same words, 'על שאנו מודים לך'. They differ only in the opening words.

phrases.english: Rav said: "We give thanks to You,

phrases.aramaic: ה׳ אֱלֹהֵינוּ עַל שֶׁאָנוּ מוֹדִים לָךְ״.
phrases.english: Lord our God, for the fact that we give thanks to You."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב מוֹדִים אֲנַחְנוּ לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מודים אנחנו לך ה׳ אלהינו על שאנו מודים לך.

steps.title: שמואל's wording
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says the people say: God of all flesh, for being able to thank You.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: God of all flesh, for the fact that we give thanks to You.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a second answer. שמואל opens with a different description of ה׳.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of 'our God', שמואל calls ה׳ the God of every living thing. The ending stays the same.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said: "God of all flesh,
for the fact that we give thanks to You."

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר אֱלֹהֵי כׇּל בָּשָׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different wording from רב's.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אלהי כל בשר על שאנו מודים לך.

steps.title: Two versions of רבי סימאי's wording
steps.stepSummary: רבי סימאי says: Our Creator, Creator of the beginning. The scholars of נהרדעא quote him differently: blessings and thanks for giving us life and keeping us alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי סימאי says: Our Creator, Who created the world at the beginning, for the fact that we give thanks to You. The scholars of נהרדעא say in the name of רבי סימאי: Blessings and thanks to Your great name, for You gave us life and kept us alive, for the fact that we give thanks to You.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי סימאי's wording, then a second tradition of what רבי סימאי said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first version praises ה׳ as Creator. The נהרדעא version thanks ה׳ for giving us life and keeping us going. These are two reports of the same teacher's words.

keyTerms.meaning: the One Who created at the beginning
the scholars of the city נהרדעא
that You gave us life and sustained us

phrases.english: Rabbi Simai says:
"Our Creator, Who created at the beginning,
for the fact that we give thanks to You."
The scholars of Nehardea say in the name of Rabbi Simai:
"Blessings and thanks to Your great name,
for You gave us life and sustained us,
for the fact that we give thanks to You."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי סִימַאי אוֹמֵר יוֹצְרֵנוּ יוֹצֵר בְּרֵאשִׁית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third wording and a second version of it.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: יוצרנו יוצר בראשית; or, in the נהרדעא version, ברכות והודאות לשמך הגדול על שהחייתנו וקיימתנו, both ending על שאנו מודים לך.

steps.title: רב אחא בר יעקב's closing words
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב ends with a request: keep us alive, gather our exiles to Your holy courtyards, so that we can serve You wholeheartedly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב finished it this way: So may You keep us alive, be kind to us, gather us, and bring our exiles to Your holy courtyards, to keep Your laws and do Your will with a whole heart, for the fact that we give thanks to You.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב adds an ending that turns the thanks into a prayer for the future.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'כן' means 'just as You gave us life before, so too do it again.' He adds a request for קיבוץ גליות and for serving ה׳ fully.

keyTerms.meaning: Your holy courtyards, of the בית המקדש

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב מְסַיֵּים בַּהּ הָכִי:
phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yaakov concludes it this way:
"So may You give us life and be gracious to us,
and gather us, and collect our exiles
to Your holy courtyards,
to keep Your laws and to do Your will
with a whole heart,
for the fact that we give thanks to You."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב מְסַיֵּים בַּהּ הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the נהרדעא version by adding a closing request.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An ending: כן תחיינו ותחננו ותקבצנו ותאסוף גליותינו לחצרות קדשך לשמור חוקיך ולעשות רצונך בלבב שלם על שאנו מודים לך.

steps.title: רב פפא: say all of them
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא concludes that since each opinion added something, we should say all the wordings together.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Therefore, let us say all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא settles the question. We do not choose one wording; we combine them all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The opinions do not contradict each other. Each one adds a different praise or request, so they can all be joined into one text. This is the source of the מודים דרבנן we say today.

keyTerms.meaning: let us say all of them

steps.whatToRemember: The מודים דרבנן that the congregation says during חזרת הש״ץ is a combination of all these אמוראים' wordings, as רב פפא ruled.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical הלכה behind a text said in every עמידה repetition today.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: הִילְכָּךְ נֵימְרִינְהוּ לְכוּלְּהוּ.
phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: Therefore, let us say all of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא הִילְכָּךְ נֵימְרִינְהוּ לְכוּלְּהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the different wordings by combining them.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The congregation says all the wordings together. This is the מודים דרבנן.

steps.title: Always respect the congregation, like the כהנים do
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק teaches that one must always have awe of the public. His proof is that the כהנים face the people and turn their backs to the שכינה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק says: Always treat the public with awe and respect. We see this from the כהנים: when they bless, they face the people and turn their backs toward the שכינה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק gives a general life rule: always show respect to the congregation. He proves it from the way the כהנים stand during ברכת כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהנים are standing in front of the ארון, where the שכינה is. You would expect them to face it. Instead they face the people, which shows how much respect the congregation deserves.

keyTerms.meaning: Awe of the public; showing the congregation real respect

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak says:
The awe of the public should always be upon you,
for the priests have their faces toward the people
and their backs toward the Divine Presence.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: לְעוֹלָם תְּהֵא אֵימַת צִבּוּר עָלֶיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic after רב פפא's conclusion about the wording the people say during מודים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One must always treat the congregation with awe and respect, as seen from the כהנים facing the people.

steps.title: A different source: דוד המלך stood up to speak to the people
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן learns respect for the congregation from a פסוק: דוד המלך stood up on his feet and called the people 'my brothers and my people.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: We learn it from here: 'Then King David stood up on his feet and said: Hear me, my brothers and my people.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives his own source for respecting the public. A king stood up to speak to the people instead of staying seated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A king usually sits while others stand before him. By standing for the people, דוד המלך showed them honor. The words 'my brothers' also come up next, and the גמרא is about to ask about them.

keyTerms.meaning: From here; we learn it from this source

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: From here:
"Then King David stood up on his feet
and said: Hear me, my brothers and my people."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר: מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different source for the same rule of respecting the public.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that one must respect the congregation.
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברי הימים א 28:2: דוד המלך stood up to address the people.

steps.title: Why both 'my brothers' and 'my people'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about the double wording in the פסוק: why does דוד say both 'my brothers' and 'my people'?
steps.simpleTranslation: If they are 'my brothers,' why say 'my people'? And if they are 'my people,' why say 'my brothers'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that the פסוק uses two different words for the people. It asks why, and this sets up רבי אלעזר's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'My brothers' is a word of equals and closeness. 'My people' is how a king speaks to his subjects. The two words seem to clash, so the גמרא wants to know what each one adds.

keyTerms.meaning: My brothers; a close, equal relationship
My people; how a king speaks to his subjects

phrases.english: If "my brothers," why "my people"?
And if "my people," why "my brothers"?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם ״אַחַי״ לָמָּה ״עַמִּי״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks closely at the wording of the פסוק רב נחמן just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the פסוק uses both 'my brothers' and 'my people'.

steps.title: Brothers if you listen, subjects if you don't
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that דוד told the people: if you listen to me willingly, you are my brothers. If not, you are my people, and I will rule you with a stick.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: דוד said to ישראל: If you listen to me, you are my brothers. If not, you are my people, and I will rule over you with a stick.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers the question about the two words. Each word fits a different situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both words are needed because they describe two possible relationships. If the people cooperate, the king treats them with warmth, like brothers. If they don't, he uses his power as king. This fits רב נחמן's point: when the people behave properly, the king relates to them with respect.

keyTerms.meaning: Listen to me; obey me willingly

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says:
David said to Israel:

phrases.aramaic: אִם אַתֶּם, שׁוֹמְעִין לִי — אַחַי אַתֶּם,
phrases.english: If you listen to me, you are my brothers;
and if not, you are my people,
and I will rule over you with a stick.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: אָמַר לָהֶם דָּוִד לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the double wording.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'My brothers' is for when the people listen willingly. 'My people' is for when they don't, and then the king rules by force.

steps.title: A third source: no sandals on the דוכן
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן bring a third source: כהנים may not go up to the דוכן in their sandals, one of the nine תקנות of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי. The גמרא suggests the reason is respect for the congregation.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן say: We learn it from here. The כהנים are not allowed to go up to the דוכן in their sandals, and this is one of the nine תקנות that רבן יוחנן בן זכאי made. What is the reason? Isn't it out of respect for the congregation?
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן offer a halachic source for respecting the public. The גמרא suggests that the rule against sandals exists so the people won't have to look at the כהנים' dirty sandals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This source would be stronger than a story, because it is an actual rule. But it works only if the reason behind the rule really is כבוד הציבור. The question 'isn't it because of respect for the congregation?' sets up that test, and רב אשי answers it next.

keyTerms.meaning: The raised platform where the כהנים stand to bless
A rule made by the חכמים

phrases.english: The Rabbis say: From here:
that the priests are not permitted
to go up to the platform in their sandals.
And this is one of the nine ordinances
that Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai instituted.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא — לָאו מִשּׁוּם כְּבוֹד צִבּוּר?
phrases.english: What is the reason? Is it not because of respect for the congregation?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּנַן אָמְרִי מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third source for the rule of respecting the public, this time from a halachic rule.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that one must respect the congregation.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The תקנה of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי that כהנים may not go up to the דוכן in sandals, assuming its reason is כבוד הציבור.

steps.title: The sandal rule has a different reason
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי rejects the proof. The real reason for the sandal rule is a worry that a strap might break. The כהן would go back to tie it and miss the blessing, and people would think he is a disqualified כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: No. There, the worry is that a strap of his sandal might snap. He would go back to tie it, and people would say: He must be the son of a גרושה or a חלוצה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי pushes back on the רבנן's proof. He says the sandal rule has nothing to do with respecting the public.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a כהן misses ברכת כהנים, onlookers might assume he was sent away because he is not a proper כהן, such as a בן גרושה or a בן חלוצה. The rule protects the כהן's family name, not the honor of the people. So the rule cannot prove כבוד הציבור.

keyTerms.meaning: Son of a כהן and a divorced woman; he is disqualified from כהונה
Son of a כהן and a woman who had חליצה; he is also disqualified

steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי is not saying that respect for the public doesn't matter. He is only saying that this particular rule has a different reason, so it cannot serve as the proof.
steps.whatToRemember: Three sources are offered for כבוד הציבור. Two stand: the כהנים facing the people (רבי יצחק), and דוד המלך standing up and calling the people 'my brothers' (רב נחמן). The third, the sandal rule from the רבנן, is rejected by רב אשי, because its real reason is to protect the כהן's reputation.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: No,

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם שֶׁמָּא נִפְסְקָה לוֹ רְצוּעָה בְּסַנְדָּלוֹ
phrases.english: there, it is lest a strap of his sandal snap
and he goes back to tie it,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי: בֶּן גְּרוּשָׁה אוֹ בֶּן חֲלוּצָה הוּא.
phrases.english: and people will say: He is the son of a divorced woman or the son of a chalutza.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the רבנן's proof by giving a different reason for the sandal rule.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the sandal rule as a source for כבוד הציבור. The principle itself stands.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The sandal rule exists to protect the כהן from false suspicion about his lineage, not to honor the congregation.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: one blessing in the מקדש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: in the מקדש, ברכת כהנים is said as one blessing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: And in the מקדש, it is one blessing, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה and quotes its next phrase. This sets up a new discussion about how ברכת כהנים was said in the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'etc.' tells us the גמרא is only quoting the opening words of the line. The next discussion will explain why the three פסוקים of ברכת כהנים were said as one blessing in the מקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc.; the rest of the line is not quoted

phrases.english: And in the Temple, one blessing, etc.
phrases.notes: This is the next line of our משנה. In the מקדש the three פסוקים were said together as one blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְמִקְדָּשׁ בְּרָכָה אַחַת
